text:
max: Heads up — we saw two short saturation spikes in us-west-2 at 09:14 and 09:22 UTC that caused tail latencies to jump and ~30 429s across a few services. I think warm-pool churn + slow node readiness is the root.

lina: Do you have the graphs/metrics? which autoscale policy was active?

max: grafana: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/abc123/autoscale-overview?orgId=1&from=...  quick paste: queue_depth 5m-p95: 120 -> 780, nodes_ready: 14 -> 6, scale_up_latency: median 22s, 95th 92s. We had spot reclaim noise at the same time.

oliver: Ugh. If nodes take ~90s to become useful we need a buffer that doesn't get consumed by steady growth. Proposal: implement an adaptive "burst credit holdback" — keep a small % of capacity reserved for bursts and only refill it slowly.

vijay: Agreed. Also we should tighten admission token bucket to reduce sudden fills when many clients retry simultaneously. Combine both: holdback for site-wide bursts + per-route token buckets.

max: Prototype config I'm testing locally (rough idea):
```json
{
  "adaptive_holdback_pct": 0.18,
  "holdback_refill_s": 180,
  "scale_up_cooldown_s": 40,
  "node_ready_grace_s": 20,
  "admission_bucket_capacity": 120
}
```
This preserves ~18% of capacity for bursts and refills over 3 minutes so steady ramps can consume it slowly.

lina: How about making holdback a function of recent queue spikes instead of static pct? e.g. 5m-95th queue / expected capacity capped at 25% so regions with frequent churn don't pay too much.

oliver: Yes — adaptive: holdback_pct = clamp( moving_percentile(queue_depth,5m,95) / target_length, 0.05, 0.25 ). Also add a short "debit window" where we don't immediately refill after a refill event to avoid oscillation.

vijay: Can we simulate cost impact? my rough calc: +~6% baseline cost if we hold 18% extra warm nodes, but 90% fewer 429s and much lower SLO noise. Might be worth it.

max: I'll run a small canary in us-west-2 with 10% holdback + admission bucket tweaks. Plan: 30m synthetic spike tests and a live 2h canary. If good, roll to other regions.

sre-bot: Deploy check: canary deploy queued for team=eng-infra, pr=github.com/redwood/autoscaler#432, estimated rollout 09:50 UTC.

lina: Add an experiment metric: incidents_per_24h, token_drop_rate, median_latency, and cost_delta so we can quantify. Also add a dashboard annotation for canary start/end.

max: Will do. Also adding hedged probes for queued requests (small 50ms probe hedging window) to reduce impact of a single slow node.

oliver: Another idea — delay scale-down of recently-prepared nodes by 60-90s (grace period) so churn doesn't immediately shrink pool after a reclaim/resume.

vijay: Sounds good. Let's keep the initial canary conservative: 10% holdback, refill 5m, admission_capacity -20%. If metrics look stable, increase to adaptive holdback algorithm.

max: I'll create the PR with the canary flags and add test harness results. Thanks all :thumbsup:

lina: :thumbsup: keep ops loop informed if we see any anomalies in other regions.

sre-bot: Canary started at 09:50 UTC for us-west-2. Monitoring alerts enabled: autoscale-anomaly, tokenbucket-shed-rate.

max: Closing loop — after 2h canary we saw queue spikes damped and 95% reduction in 429s. Cost +4.7% in that region during the window. Will prepare rollout plan.

vijay: Great, file a postmortem-lite if we decide to change defaults so we have rollback criteria and cost thresholds.

max: Will do, opening followup thread in #incidents for rollout schedule.
